title: Tale of Khalbas and his Wife and the Learned Man (தமிழ்)

full_text:
In Damascus lived an honest weaver named Khalbas, whose wife was celebrated for her sharp practical wit and domestic management. A self-important traveling scholar visited their home, boasting loudly at the supper table of his supreme erudition in logic and philosophy, treating the weaver and his wife as ignorant peasants.

The scholar pontificated: 'Through logic, I can prove that the two roasted pigeons upon this platter are actually three!'

The wife smiled pleasantly: 'Show us your demonstration, learned master.'

The scholar declared: 'Here is the first pigeon, and here is the second pigeon; and one added to two equals three! Therefore, there are three pigeons upon the platter!'

The wife immediately took the first pigeon and placed it on her husband’s plate, saying: 'Khalbas, take the first pigeon.' She then took the second pigeon and placed it upon her own plate: 'And I shall take the second pigeon.'

She then turned to the astonished scholar with a courteous smile: 'And you, learned master, may feast upon the third pigeon that your logic has created!'

The scholar sat before his empty plate, blushing with profound shame amidst the hearty laughter of the household.

He apologized for his pedantic arrogance, and the wife generously shared her meal with him, having taught him that philosophical logic must never lose touch with practical reality and humble manners.
moral: A household thrives on mutual respect and shared intellect, not arrogant displays of pedantry. [TA]
